dissents.topic: Whether the import ordering in tests/test_cmd_inspect_app.py is a problem

positions.position: The import order violates isort/PEP8 conventions used elsewhere; `import contextlib` is incorrectly slotted between `from argparse import Namespace` and `import io`. The project's linter will likely flag this — run the formatter.
The ordering matches the existing file's convention (mixed 'from' and 'import' sorted lexicographically by module name) and is consistent. No action required if tox passes.

dissents.topic: Whether a parity test against contextlib is needed

positions.position: A one-liner asserting `contextlib.redirect_stdout` produces the same captured output would close the loop and demonstrate the patch's rationale. Not blocking, but if you're adding a test, add the one that proves the rationale.
The test is the right shape as-is — it confirms the value (captured stdout) and warning identity flow correctly during the deprecation window. No change needed.
Parity is not the missing piece; what's missing is exercising the stderr branch and the simultaneous-both case to lock in the deprecated contract.

dissents.topic: Whether the runtime warning text is precise enough

positions.position: The warning text 'This context manager is deprecated' fails to name the function (should say 'falcon.testing.redirected is deprecated...') so logs without tracebacks are ambiguous.
The warning is precise but omits the deprecation origin version (4.3); it states only the removal milestone (5.0). The deprecation contract should be uniform across runtime and docs.
The warning omits the behavioral contract difference — that contextlib.redirect_stdout/stderr cover only one stream each, so callers using the dual-stream form cannot do a 1:1 substitution.
The warning and the docstring directive duplicate the same text in two places, which will drift over time.

issues.description: Docstring typo: 'stlib' should be 'stdlib' in the deprecation directive
issues.detail: The added `.. deprecated:: 4.3` block in the docstring reads 'Use the stlib's :func:`contextlib.redirect_stdout`...'. This typo appears in user-facing documentation — the one signpost from old to new — and will render in the published docs. Trivial one-line fix while touching the file.

issues.description: Deprecation warning text omits 'falcon.testing.' prefix when naming the affected function
issues.detail: The runtime warning says 'This context manager is deprecated' without naming `falcon.testing.redirected`. A reader who catches the warning in a log without a traceback won't know which context manager is meant. Making the message self-describing ('falcon.testing.redirected is deprecated...') improves diagnostic readability.

issues.description: Deprecation message and migration docs do not show the dual-stream substitution pattern for contextlib
issues.detail: falcon.testing.redirected accepts both stdout and stderr in a single call and restores both. contextlib.redirect_stdout and redirect_stderr each cover only one stream, so callers using the dual-stream form must nest two managers or use ExitStack. The deprecation message, docstring, and newsfragment all point users to contextlib but do not document this non-1:1 substitution, even though the harder case is not exercised by internal call sites.

issues.description: Deprecation runtime warning omits the deprecation origin version (4.3)
issues.detail: The runtime warning says 'will be removed in Falcon 5.0' but does not state the version in which deprecation began (4.3). The `.. deprecated:: 4.3` directive carries it in docs; the runtime surface does not. Specification of the deprecation contract should be uniform across runtime and documentation surfaces.

issues.description: Deprecation message duplicates information already in the docstring directive
issues.detail: The runtime warning string and the `.. deprecated:: 4.3` docstring directive carry overlapping text in two locations, which will drift over time. Keeping a canonical source and referencing it would be cleaner.

issues.description: Test does not exercise the stderr branch of the deprecated contract
issues.detail: test_deprecated_redirected verifies only the stdout path. The redirected() ADT promises redirection of stderr as well, and (per Liskov) the deprecation must not silently change behavior for either stream before 5.0. Adding a stderr assertion — ideally the simultaneous-both case — would lock in the contract for the remainder of the deprecation window.

issues.description: Test does not verify that sys.stdout/sys.stderr are restored after the context exits (invariant of redirected())
issues.detail: The new test exercises the happy path: warning fires, captured output matches. The structural invariant of the context manager — that sys.stdout == old_stdout in the finally branch even on exception — is not asserted. Since this is the last test that will exist for this function before removal, locking in the restoration invariant has value.

issues.description: Test does not assert parity with contextlib (the patch's stated rationale)
issues.detail: The entire claim of the patch is that contextlib does the same thing as redirected(), but there's no test asserting parity. A short assertion that `contextlib.redirect_stdout` produces equivalent captured output would close the loop on the rationale. Not blocking — stdlib carries its own tests — but the test that proves the migration claim is missing.

issues.description: Test does not document that it is preserving the dual obligation (warning fires AND deprecated semantics still hold)
issues.detail: test_deprecated_redirected asserts both that the warning fires and that output.getvalue() == 'test output\n', but the dual obligation is incidental rather than stated. A brief comment naming the invariant ('deprecated path remains semantically equivalent until 5.0') would make the contract explicit rather than implicit.

issues.description: Import order in tests/test_cmd_inspect_app.py is suspicious — disputed
issues.detail: The new import sequence is `from argparse import Namespace`, `import contextlib`, `import io`, `import sys`. Torvalds reads this as an isort/PEP8 violation that mixes 'from' and plain 'import' lines and will likely be auto-fixed or flagged by tox. Dijkstra reads this as consistent with the existing file's lexicographic-by-module convention and therefore fine if tox passes. Either way, run the formatter to make it unambiguous.

issues.description: Decomposition direction is correct: retiring the wrapper in favor of stdlib (informational)
issues.detail: falcon.testing.redirected was a thin wrapper around stdlib functionality that has existed since Python 3.4/3.5. Keeping it complected falcon's testing identity with a stdlib concern that has its own evolution. Pointing users to contextlib is the right simplification — less code in falcon, the capability lives where it belongs. No action required; recorded for completeness.

synthesis.summary: All six reviewers converge: this is a small, well-scoped deprecation that correctly retires a thin wrapper (falcon.testing.redirected) in favor of stdlib contextlib equivalents, with the decorator, docstring directive, news fragment, internal migrations, and a happy-path test all in place. The single universally flagged defect is the 'stlib' typo in the user-facing deprecation docstring directive — every reviewer caught it. Beyond the typo, concerns cluster around three themes: the runtime warning is under-specified (Knuth wants the function named, Dijkstra wants the 4.3 origin version, Liskov wants the non-1:1 dual-stream substitution documented, Pike notes duplicated text), the test could go further (Liskov/Pike want stderr coverage, Torvalds wants contextlib parity, Knuth wants restoration-on-exception, Dijkstra wants the invariant stated explicitly), and there is a live disagreement between Torvalds and Dijkstra over whether the import order in test_cmd_inspect_app.py is a formatter violation or simply consistent with the file's existing convention. No P0 or P1 issues; the panel's strongest preserved disagreement is the import-order question, and the strongest preserved minority concern is Liskov's point that the advertised substitution to contextlib is not actually substitutable for dual-stream callers without nesting.
